question: Should OpenClaw accept the experimental Claw lifecycle as a core-owned, durable workspace-management feature and continue reviewing this stacked workspace-file slice?
rationale: The patch is not a repair of an established contract: it creates a new consented lifecycle, persistent ownership ledger, and package-to-agent instruction boundary. Only maintainers can decide whether that product and ownership model belongs in core.

options.title: Pause pending sponsorship
options.body: Keep the protected stack open but do not merge or dispatch further repair work until an authorized maintainer confirms this RFC direction.

options.title: Sponsor the lifecycle
options.body: Accept the experimental core direction, then review and land the prerequisite workspace/root-provenance slice before this dependent file-owner slice.

options.title: Decline core ownership
options.body: Close the implementation stack and redirect any narrower reusable pieces through existing plugin or package seams where appropriate.

recommendation.title: Pause pending sponsorship
recommendation.body: Keep the protected stack open but do not merge or dispatch further repair work until an authorized maintainer confirms this RFC direction.

likelyOwner.reason: Shared-state and core-lifecycle history make this the strongest available routing candidate for the sponsorship decision.
